questions.q: Which AI use cases are in production, and which ones worry you most?
questions.why: Starts from real use, not from the AI policy.
questions.need: The AI use cases in production are known, with the riskiest named
questions.how: List them with their owners and rank by what they can touch
questions.listen: Named use cases with an owner; "a few pilots" usually means more in production than anyone listed.
questions.probe: Which of them answer customers, or change something on their own?

questions.q: How would you find out about a team using a new model or AI service?
questions.why: Unapproved AI use is the norm before inventory exists.
questions.need: A new model or AI service is seen when a team starts using it
questions.how: Watch for AI services in cloud accounts and on the network
questions.listen: Through spend, network or sign-in; "someone would tell us" means nobody would.
questions.probe: When did security last learn about an AI service after it was already in use?

questions.q: Do you know which agents can call tools, and what those tools can change?
questions.why: An agent is as dangerous as the permissions of its tools.
questions.need: What each agent can call, and change, is known
questions.how: List agents with their tools and the permissions behind them
questions.listen: Agents that can change things matter more than chat: list the tools and what each can do.
questions.probe: Which agent could change a record, send a message or spend money?

questions.q: Are prompts and responses logged anywhere you could investigate?
questions.why: Without logs, an AI incident cannot be reconstructed.
questions.need: Prompts and responses can be investigated
questions.how: Log them where security can search them, with retention agreed
questions.listen: Logged and searchable for the time an investigation needs; otherwise an incident cannot be explained.
questions.probe: If an answer caused harm last week, could you find the prompt behind it?

questions.q: What stops sensitive data from being pasted into a prompt or indexed for retrieval?
questions.why: Data leaves through prompts and vector stores, not only through files.
questions.need: Sensitive data cannot reach a prompt or a retrieval index unseen
questions.how: Put a data check in front of prompts and indexing
questions.listen: A check before the prompt or the index; a policy alone is a hope.
questions.probe: Which data would be worst to see in a prompt, and what stops it today?

questions.q: Who owns the keys to model providers, and when were they last rotated?
questions.why: Shared, long-lived keys are the usual weak point.
questions.need: Model provider keys have an owner and are rotated
questions.how: Move keys to a vault and set a rotation date
questions.listen: Keys with an owner, scoped and rotated; keys in code or shared by teams are the usual finding.
questions.probe: Where do those keys live today, and who can read them?

questions.q: Has anyone tried to break your models or agents on purpose?
questions.why: Adversarial testing finds what guardrails miss.
questions.need: Models and agents have been tested by someone trying to break them
questions.how: Run one red-team exercise on the riskiest use case
questions.listen: Tested by someone trying to break them, with the results fixed; "not yet" is common and honest.
questions.probe: What would an agent do with an instruction hidden in a document it reads?

questions.q: Which regulation or customer question about AI do you need to answer this year?
questions.why: Gives the work a deadline and a sponsor.
questions.need: The AI regulation or customer question due this year has an answer
questions.how: Name the question, the owner and the evidence it needs
questions.listen: A regulation or a customer's questionnaire with a date makes this urgent.
questions.probe: Who has to sign the answer, and by when?
